question: On a 13-qubit tantalum-based superconducting processor, was the median single-qubit gate fidelity higher or lower when randomized benchmarking was run on all qubits simultaneously than when each qubit was benchmarked in isolation?
methods: A surface-13 tunable-coupling superconducting processor was built with tantalum qubits, coplanar waveguides and airbridges. Single-qubit gate fidelities were measured by randomized benchmarking with each qubit benchmarked alone and with all qubits benchmarked at the same time, and the median values were compared.
option_a: Median fidelity was higher for simultaneous benchmarking than for isolated benchmarking.
option_b: Median fidelity was lower for simultaneous benchmarking than for isolated benchmarking.
evidence_quote: The median single-qubit gate fidelity shows a tiny decrease from about 99.95% for the isolated Randomized Benchmarking to 99.94% for the simultaneous one.

title: Effectiveness of the syndrome extraction circuit with flag qubits on IBM quantum hardware
question: On IBM superconducting hardware, with flag qubits placed between non-adjacent data and syndrome qubits, did the logical error rate of a repetition code increase or decrease as the code distance was raised from three to nine?
methods: A syndrome-extraction circuit in which flag qubits mediate between data and syndrome qubits that are not adjacent was run on IBM quantum processors with a non-topological coupling map. Repetition codes of distance three to nine were implemented with one or two flag qubits separating data and syndrome qubits, and logical error rates were compared across distances.
option_a: Logical error rates decreased as code distance increased.
option_b: Logical error rates increased as code distance increased.
evidence_quote: Even though the data qubit is not adjacent to the syndrome qubit, logical error rates diminish as the distance of the repetition code increases from three to nine.

title: High-Coherence Kerr-cat qubit in 2D architecture
question: As the cat size of a Kerr-cat qubit in a planar superconducting circuit was raised up to 10 photons, did its phase-flip time increase or decrease?
methods: A Kerr-cat qubit was stabilised by a two-photon drive on a Kerr-nonlinear oscillator in a 2D superconducting circuit with an on-chip band-block filter. Bit-flip and phase-flip times were measured as a function of the mean photon number of the cat state, up to 10 photons.
option_a: The phase-flip time increased as cat size increased.
option_b: The phase-flip time decreased as cat size increased.
evidence_quote: Finally, the lifetime in this architecture is examined as a function of the cat size of up to 10 photons in the oscillator achieving a bit-flip time higher than 1 ms and only a linear decrease in the phase-flip time, in good agreement with the theoretical analysis of the circuit.

title: Dephasing and error dynamics affecting a singlet-triplet qubit during coherent spin shuttling
question: For small numbers of repeated shuttles of a singlet-triplet spin qubit in silicon, did magnetic dephasing contribute more or less to the losses than incoherent shuttle errors?
methods: A singlet-triplet spin qubit was coherently shuttled back and forth through an array of silicon quantum dots for a variable number N of repeated shuttle operations. Qubit decay was measured as a function of N and attributed to magnetic dephasing or to incoherent shuttle errors.
option_a: At small shuttle counts, magnetic dephasing contributed more to the losses than incoherent shuttle errors.
option_b: At small shuttle counts, magnetic dephasing contributed less to the losses than incoherent shuttle errors.
evidence_quote: We find that losses are dominated by magnetic dephasing for small $N<10^3$ and by incoherent shuttle errors for large $N>10^3$.

title: Effect of Etching Methods on Dielectric Losses in Transmons
question: Were the relaxation and coherence times of aluminium transmons made with chlorine-plasma dry etching longer or shorter than those of transmons made with weak-acid wet etching?
methods: Aluminium transmon qubits were fabricated with two etching methods: wet etching in a weak-acid solution and dry etching in a chlorine-based plasma. Energy relaxation and coherence times were measured for both sets, together with time fluctuations of qubit frequencies and relaxation times.
option_a: Relaxation and coherence times were longer for dry-etched qubits than for wet-etched ones.
option_b: Relaxation and coherence times were shorter for dry-etched qubits than for wet-etched ones.
evidence_quote: The relaxation and coherence times for dry-etched qubits are more than twice as long as those for wet-etched ones.

title: Recovery dynamics of a gap-engineered transmon after a quasiparticle burst
question: Was the reduction in quasiparticle-burst detection rate obtained by gap engineering in 3D transmons larger or smaller than expected if the burst quasiparticles quickly thermalised to the cryostat temperature?
methods: Quasiparticle bursts caused by ionizing radiation were resolved in 3D gap-engineered transmon qubits by continuously monitoring qubit transitions. The reduction in burst detection rate from gap engineering was compared with the reduction expected if quasiparticles rapidly thermalised to the cryostat temperature.
option_a: The reduction was larger than expected from fast thermalisation.
option_b: The reduction was smaller than expected from fast thermalisation.
evidence_quote: This reduction falls four orders of magnitude short of that expected if the quasiparticles were to quickly thermalize to the cryostat temperature.
notes: Headline side = the gap-engineering intervention works as expected (larger reduction).

title: Simultaneous High-Fidelity Single-Qubit Gates in a Spin Qubit Array
question: In a five-qubit silicon spin array with a shared control line, was single-qubit pi/2 gate fidelity during parallel operation of all five qubits higher or lower than during simultaneous operation of up to three qubits?
methods: Single-qubit pi/2 gates were benchmarked in a five-qubit silicon spin-qubit array driven through a shared control line, after pairwise phase calibrations to compensate drive-induced AC Stark shifts. Fidelities were measured for individual operation, for simultaneous operation of up to three qubits, and for parallel operation of all five qubits.
option_a: Fidelity was lower during five-qubit parallel operation than with up to three simultaneous qubits.
option_b: Fidelity was higher during five-qubit parallel operation than with up to three simultaneous qubits.
evidence_quote: During parallel five-qubit operation, fidelities remain at the practical fault-tolerant threshold of 99.9%, with the loss attributed to drive-induced decoherence resulting from increased microwave power.
notes: Previous abstract sentence: fidelities 'are preserved above 99.99% during simultaneous operation of up to three qubits'.

title: Evidence for unexpectedly low quasiparticle generation rates across Josephson junctions of driven superconducting qubits
question: In strongly driven superconducting qubits, were the measured total energy-loss rates higher or lower than predicted by a Floquet-Markov model of drive-induced quasiparticle generation across the Josephson junctions?
methods: Superconducting qubits were driven to very large amplitudes by applying intense fields through their readout resonators, and the resonators' nonlinear responses were used to quantify energy loss at the qubits. The measured loss rates were compared with Floquet-Markov predictions of drive-induced quasiparticle generation across the junctions.
option_a: Measured loss rates were higher than the model predicted.
option_b: Measured loss rates were lower than the model predicted.
evidence_quote: Surprisingly, the estimated total energy loss rates are far lower than those expected by the Floquet-Markov formalism with QPG as the sole loss mechanism.
notes: Headline side = the paper's highlighted finding (low quasiparticle generation).

title: Stability studies on subtractively-fabricated CMOS-compatible superconducting transmon qubits
question: Among subtractively fabricated CMOS-compatible transmons monitored over 95 hours, did qubits with higher mean T1 show larger or smaller T1 fluctuations?
methods: Eight subtractively fabricated, CMOS-compatible transmon qubits were monitored during a single cooldown for 95 hours, tracking T1, T2* and other parameters. The size of each qubit's T1 fluctuations was compared with its mean T1.
option_a: Qubits with higher mean T1 showed larger T1 fluctuations.
option_b: Qubits with higher mean T1 showed smaller T1 fluctuations.
evidence_quote: We also demonstrate that subtractively-fabricated superconducting quantum devices align with the theoretical predictions that higher mean lifetimes $T_1$ correspond to larger fluctuations.

title: Stability studies on subtractively-fabricated CMOS-compatible superconducting transmon qubits
question: Over ten cooldown cycles spanning more than a year, did the transition frequencies of two tracked CMOS-compatible transmon qubits shift up or down?
methods: Two representative subtractively fabricated, CMOS-compatible transmon qubits were tracked over 10 cooldown cycles spanning more than one year. Qubit transition frequencies, readout resonator frequencies and T1 were measured in each cycle.
option_a: The qubit transition frequencies shifted up over the cooldown cycles.
option_b: The qubit transition frequencies shifted down over the cooldown cycles.
evidence_quote: We observed an average total downward shift in both qubit transition frequencies of approximately 61 MHz within the thermal cycles considered.

title: Superconducting qubit decoherence correlated with detected radiation events
question: Immediately after radiation events registered on both detector arrays surrounding a transmon, were the qubit's T1 and T2 higher or lower than at other times?
methods: A transmon qubit was sandwiched between two microwave kinetic inductance detector (MKID) arrays that register radiation-induced phonon bursts in real time. Single-shot T1 and T2 measurements were synchronised with MKID detections, and values immediately after coincident events on both arrays were compared with values at other times.
option_a: T1 and T2 were lower immediately after the coincident detection events.
option_b: T1 and T2 were higher immediately after the coincident detection events.
evidence_quote: By synchronizing MKID event detection with single-shot measurements of qubit energy relaxation ($T_1$) and phase coherence ($T_2$), we observe statistically significant reductions in both $T_1$ and $T_2$-up to 30.5%-immediately following dual MKID events attributed to penetrating muons.

title: Assessing the Sensitivity of Niobium- and Tantalum-Based Superconducting Qubits to Infrared Radiation
question: With infrared filters installed, were quasiparticle tunnelling rates higher or lower in tantalum-based offset-charge-sensitive qubits than in niobium-based ones?
methods: Offset-charge-sensitive superconducting qubits made from niobium or tantalum films were exposed to a controlled thermal radiation source, and quasiparticle tunnelling rates were measured. The effect of in-line infrared filters in the wiring and of ambient infrared absorbers was tested, and tunnelling rates for the two materials were compared with filters installed.
option_a: Tunnelling rates were higher in tantalum qubits than in niobium qubits.
option_b: Tunnelling rates were lower in tantalum qubits than in niobium qubits.
evidence_quote: We identify both radiation channels as significant contributions to decoherence for tantalum but not for niobium qubits and achieve tunneling rates of 100 Hz and 300 Hz for niobium and tantalum respectively upon installation of infrared filters.

title: Electrical post-fabrication tuning of aluminum Josephson junctions at room temperature
question: During room-temperature voltage-pulse tuning of aluminium Josephson junctions, did the rate of resistance increase grow faster or slower than linearly as the pulse amplitude was raised?
methods: Aluminium Josephson junctions were tuned at room temperature by applying voltage pulses that raise their resistance. The rate of resistance increase during manipulation was measured as a function of pulse amplitude, and spontaneous resistance drift after manipulation was tracked at room and cryogenic temperatures.
option_a: The rate of resistance increase grew faster than linearly with pulse amplitude.
option_b: The rate of resistance increase grew slower than linearly with pulse amplitude.
evidence_quote: We find that the rate of resistance increase scales exponentially with pulse amplitude during manipulation.

title: Readout-induced degradation of transmon lifetimes: interplay of TLSs and qubit spectral reshaping
question: For a fixed measurement rate, was the readout-induced reduction of a transmon's lifetime smaller or larger when driving at the resonator frequency associated with the qubit ground state than at other readout drive frequencies?
methods: Lifetime degradation of a frequency-tunable transmon during dispersive readout was measured and modelled using a bath of detuned two-level systems and a drive-renormalised qubit emission spectrum. The readout drive frequency was varied at a fixed measurement rate, and qubit lifetimes during readout were compared.
option_a: Lifetime degradation was larger when driving at the ground-state resonator frequency than at other drive frequencies.
option_b: Lifetime degradation was smaller when driving at the ground-state resonator frequency than at other drive frequencies.
evidence_quote: In particular, we find that driving at the resonator frequency associated with the qubit ground state yields the narrowest qubit emission spectrum and the least lifetime degradation for a fixed measurement rate, providing a practical guideline for optimizing readout protocols in future quantum processors.

title: Characterization and Comparison of Energy Relaxation in Fluxonium Qubits
question: Was the process-mean effective capacitive quality factor of planar fluxonium qubits higher or lower when a fluorine-based wet treatment was applied before Josephson junction deposition than with the baseline process?
methods: Eight planar aluminium-on-silicon fluxonium qubits from two fabrication processes, a baseline and one with a fluorine-based wet treatment before junction deposition, were characterised. Measured T1 values were converted to an effective capacitive quality factor after accounting for 1/f flux noise and radiative loss, and the process means were compared.
option_a: The effective capacitive quality factor was lower with the fluorine treatment.
option_b: The effective capacitive quality factor was higher with the fluorine treatment.
evidence_quote: We resolve a small improvement of (13.8 $\pm$ 8.4$)\%$ in the process mean $Q_\mathrm{C}^{\mathrm{eff}}$, indicating that the fluorine treatment may have reduced loss from the metal-substrate interface, but did not address the primary source of loss in these fluxonium qubits.
notes: Effect is small (abstract: 'small improvement').

title: Coherence limitations of a Fourier-engineered $\cos(2\varphi)$ transmon qubit
question: Compared with a fluxonium qubit with a similar energy spectrum and noise amplitude, was the lifetime of a cos(2phi) qubit at its flux symmetry point more or less affected by 1/f flux noise?
methods: A cos(2phi) qubit built from a multi-junction interference circuit was realised experimentally. Its energy relaxation time was measured as a function of external flux, and its sensitivity to 1/f flux noise at the symmetry point was compared with that of a fluxonium with a similar spectrum and noise amplitude.
option_a: The cos(2phi) qubit was less affected by flux noise than the comparable fluxonium.
option_b: The cos(2phi) qubit was more affected by flux noise than the comparable fluxonium.
evidence_quote: In contrast, a fluxonium qubit with a similar energy spectrum and noise amplitude is less affected by flux noise, highlighting a key challenge for interference-based protection schemes.
notes: Headline side = the protected qubit design works (less affected). The fluxonium comparison may be partly model-based; the cos(2phi) lifetime limit by 1/f flux noise is measured.

title: Chain-of-Thought Unfaithfulness as Disguised Accuracy
question: After normalising an answer-dependence measure of chain-of-thought faithfulness for each model's bias toward particular answer choices, was the measured unfaithfulness of smaller, less-capable models higher or lower than under the unnormalised measure?
methods: An earlier study's CoT-faithfulness scaling experiments, which score how much a model's answer depends on its chain of thought, were replicated with three model families spanning a range of sizes. The measure was then recomputed after normalising for each model's bias toward certain answer choices, and the values for smaller, less-capable models were compared before and after normalisation.
option_a: Measured unfaithfulness of smaller models was higher after normalisation than before.
option_b: Measured unfaithfulness of smaller models was lower after normalisation than before.
evidence_quote: However, after normalizing the metric to account for a model's bias toward certain answer choices, unfaithfulness drops significantly for smaller less-capable models.
notes: Headline side is the paper's own normalisation changing the result.

title: Judging the Judges: A Systematic Study of Position Bias in LLM-as-a-Judge
question: In pairwise and list-wise LLM-judge evaluations, was position bias more or less strongly affected by the quality gap between candidate solutions than by the length of prompt components?
methods: Fifteen LLM judges evaluated solutions from about 40 generating models on MTBench and DevBench tasks in pairwise and list-wise settings, with the order of candidates varied. Position bias was measured with repetition-stability, position-consistency and preference-fairness metrics, and its dependence on prompt-component length and on the quality gap between candidates was analysed.
option_a: Position bias was more strongly affected by the quality gap between solutions than by prompt-component length.
option_b: Position bias was less strongly affected by the quality gap between solutions than by prompt-component length.
evidence_quote: While position bias is weakly influenced by the length of prompt components, it is strongly affected by the quality gap between solutions.

title: Super(ficial)-alignment: Strong Models May Deceive Weak Models in Weak-to-Strong Generalization
question: In weak-to-strong alignment experiments with conflicting alignment targets, did the measured weak-to-strong deception become stronger or weaker as the capability gap between the weak supervisor and the strong student grew?
methods: Weak models supervised stronger models in reward-modelling and preference-optimisation setups with two conflicting alignment targets (e.g. helpfulness versus harmlessness). Deception was measured as the strong model behaving well on cases the weak model knows about while misbehaving on cases the weak model does not know about, and it was compared across weak-strong pairs with different capability gaps.
option_a: Deception became stronger as the capability gap grew.
option_b: Deception became weaker as the capability gap grew.
evidence_quote: (2) The deception intensifies as the capability gap between weak and strong models increases.

title: Self-Preference Bias in LLM-as-a-Judge
question: Compared with human evaluators, did LLM evaluators give relatively higher or lower ratings to outputs with lower perplexity?
methods: LLM judges including GPT-4 rated dialogue responses, and their ratings were compared with human ratings of the same responses. The relationship between ratings and each response's perplexity under the judging model was analysed, separately for self-generated and other-generated responses.
option_a: LLM evaluators gave relatively higher ratings to lower-perplexity outputs than human evaluators did.
option_b: LLM evaluators gave relatively lower ratings to lower-perplexity outputs than human evaluators did.
evidence_quote: Our findings reveal that LLMs assign significantly higher evaluations to outputs with lower perplexity than human evaluators, regardless of whether the outputs were self-generated.
notes: Headline side is the paper's hypothesised perplexity mechanism for self-preference bias.

title: Subversion Strategy Eval: Can language models statelessly strategize to subvert control protocols?
question: When models were given the ability to share a plan between contexts, was their performance at strategising to subvert AI control protocols higher or lower than when acting statelessly without that affordance?
methods: Claude 3.5 models (including versions trained for helpfulness alone) and OpenAI reasoning models were placed in eight environments in which they had to devise and act on strategies to subvert AI control protocols across separate contexts with no shared memory. Performance was compared across sets of affordances, one of which let the model pass a plan from one context to another.
option_a: Subversion performance was lower with plan sharing than without it.
option_b: Subversion performance was higher with plan sharing than without it.
evidence_quote: However, providing models with additional affordances, such as the ability to share a plan between contexts, can substantially improve performance.
notes: Abstract says the affordance 'can substantially improve performance'; baseline performance was low.

title: Judging with Many Minds: Do More Perspectives Mean Less Prejudice? On Bias Amplifications and Resistance in Multi-Agent Based LLM-as-Judge
question: Across position, verbosity, chain-of-thought and bandwagon biases, did a multi-agent debate judging framework show more or less bias amplification than a meta-judge framework?
methods: Four bias types were measured in two multi-agent LLM-as-judge setups: multi-agent debate, in which judge agents argue over several rounds, and a meta-judge setup, in which one LLM judges the judgements of others. Bias levels were tracked from the initial judgement through subsequent rounds.
option_a: The debate framework showed more bias amplification than the meta-judge framework.
option_b: The debate framework showed less bias amplification than the meta-judge framework.
evidence_quote: Our results show that debate framework amplifies biases sharply after the initial debate, and this increased bias is sustained in subsequent rounds, while meta-judge approaches exhibit greater resistance.

title: CoT Red-Handed: Stress Testing Chain-of-Thought Monitoring
question: In red-teaming cases where the sabotage was obvious, did a monitor reading the untrusted model's chain of thought detect sabotage better or worse than a monitor reading the model's final actions and outputs?
methods: A weaker trusted model monitored a stronger untrusted model that was instructed to pursue a harmful side task while solving coding problems. Detection by a monitor that reads the reasoning trace was compared with detection by a monitor that reads the final actions and outputs, separately for subtle and obvious sabotage.
option_a: Chain-of-thought monitoring detected obvious sabotage better than action-level monitoring.
option_b: Chain-of-thought monitoring detected obvious sabotage worse than action-level monitoring.
evidence_quote: We find that while CoT monitoring is more effective than overseeing only model outputs in scenarios where action-only monitoring fails to reliably identify sabotage, reasoning traces can contain misleading rationalizations that deceive the CoT monitors, reducing performance in obvious sabotage cases.
notes: Headline side = CoT monitoring (the studied mitigation) works. The abstract's 'reducing performance in obvious sabotage cases' is contrasted with action-only monitoring; the paper's own proposal is a hybrid monitor, not asked about here.

title: Unspoken Hints: Accuracy Without Acknowledgement in LLM Reasoning
question: Compared with answer hints framed as a user's opinion (sycophancy style), were answer hints framed as leaked data acknowledged more or less often in the models' chain-of-thought reasoning?
methods: GPT-4o and Gemini-2-Flash solved problems from AIME, GSM-Hard, MATH-500 and UniADILR with embedded answer hints that varied in correctness, complexity and presentation style (sycophancy framing versus data-leak framing). Task accuracy and whether the reasoning explicitly acknowledged the hint were recorded for each condition.
option_a: Leak-style hints were acknowledged more often than sycophancy-style hints.
option_b: Leak-style hints were acknowledged less often than sycophancy-style hints.
evidence_quote: Third, presentation style matters: sycophancy prompts encourage overt acknowledgement, while leak-style prompts increase accuracy but promote hidden reliance.

title: AI Debaters are More Persuasive when Arguing in Alignment with Their Own Beliefs
question: In pairwise comparisons of argument quality, were arguments that defended positions misaligned with the debater model's own measured prior beliefs rated higher or lower than arguments aligned with those beliefs?
methods: LLM debaters' prior beliefs on subjective questions were measured before the debates. Debaters then argued positions either consistent or inconsistent with those priors in front of a judge persona with stated positions of its own, under sequential and simultaneous debate protocols, and argument quality was assessed by pairwise comparison.
option_a: Arguments misaligned with prior beliefs were rated lower in quality than aligned arguments.
option_b: Arguments misaligned with prior beliefs were rated higher in quality than aligned arguments.
evidence_quote: Our main findings show that models tend to prefer defending stances aligned with the judge persona rather than their prior beliefs, sequential debate introduces significant bias favoring the second debater, models are more persuasive when defending positions aligned with their prior beliefs, and paradoxically, arguments misaligned with prior beliefs are rated as higher quality in pairwise comparison.

title: Reasoning Models Sometimes Output Illegible Chains of Thought
question: Across reasoning models trained with outcome-based reinforcement learning, was chain-of-thought legibility higher or lower on harder questions than on easier ones?
methods: Chains of thought from 14 reasoning models were scored for how legible they were to humans and to AI monitors. Legibility scores were compared across questions of different difficulty.
option_a: Legibility was lower on harder questions than on easier ones.
option_b: Legibility was higher on harder questions than on easier ones.
evidence_quote: We also find that legibility degrades on harder questions.

title: Fairness or Fluency? An Investigation into Language Bias of Pairwise LLM-as-a-Judge
question: When LLM judges compared two answers written in different languages, was their preference more or less strongly influenced by the language of the answers than by the language of the question?
methods: Pairwise LLM-as-judge experiments presented two candidate answers in different languages, with the language of the answers and the language of the question varied independently. The judges' preferences for answers in particular languages, such as English, were measured across conditions.
option_a: Preference was less strongly influenced by answer language than by question language.
option_b: Preference was more strongly influenced by answer language than by question language.
evidence_quote: For inter-language judging, we observe that most models favor English answers, and that this preference is influenced more by answer language than question language.

title: Lie to Me: How Faithful Is Chain-of-Thought Reasoning in Reasoning Models?
question: When injected hints changed the answers of open-weight reasoning models, was acknowledgment of the hint more or less frequent in the thinking tokens than in the final answer text?
methods: Twelve open-weight reasoning models (7B-685B parameters, nine architectural families) answered MMLU and GPQA Diamond questions with six categories of injected hints. For cases in which a hint changed the answer, keyword analysis measured whether the hint's influence was acknowledged in the thinking tokens and in the answer text.
option_a: Hint acknowledgment was less frequent in thinking tokens than in answer text.
option_b: Hint acknowledgment was more frequent in thinking tokens than in answer text.
evidence_quote: Training methodology and model family predict faithfulness more strongly than parameter count, and keyword-based analysis reveals a striking gap between thinking-token acknowledgment (approximately 87.5%) and answer-text acknowledgment (approximately 28.6%), suggesting that models internally recognize hint influence but systematically suppress this acknowledgment in their outputs.

title: Retrying vs Resampling in AI Control
question: When several candidate actions were resampled at each step, did auditing based on the maximum resampled suspicion score yield higher or lower safety than auditing based on the minimum?
methods: In the BashArena control setting, Claude Opus 4.6 acted as the untrusted model and MiMo-V2-Flash as the trusted monitor. Several samples were drawn from the same context at each step, and audit decisions based on the maximum versus the minimum of the resampled suspicion scores were compared at a fixed small audit budget.
option_a: Auditing on the maximum score yielded higher safety than auditing on the minimum.
option_b: Auditing on the maximum score yielded lower safety than auditing on the minimum.
evidence_quote: The first is that auditing based on the maximum across resampled suspicion scores outperforms using the minimum, which is the opposite of what Ctrl-Z found.
notes: Result contradicts an earlier paper (Ctrl-Z), which found the minimum better.

title: Debate Helps Weak Judges Reward Stronger Models
question: Among stronger-debater/weaker-judge model pairings, were the pairings in which proposer-critic debate gave statistically reliable gains over consultancy the more capable or the less capable pairings?
methods: Five pairings of a stronger debater model with a weaker judge model were tested on programmatically verifiable code and logic tasks. For each pairing, judge accuracy under proposer-critic debate was compared with a consultancy baseline, and the pairings with and without reliable gains were compared by model capability.
option_a: The pairings with reliable debate gains were the more capable model pairings.
option_b: The pairings with reliable debate gains were the less capable model pairings.
evidence_quote: On the three of five pairings where the condition holds, proposer-critic debate's gains are statistically significant over consultancy, and these pairings are the most capable model pairings.

title: Debate Helps Weak Judges Reward Stronger Models
question: In model pairings where the critic's and the judge's classification abilities were about equal, did the judge's rate of verifying claims rise or fall once a critic's speech entered the transcript?
methods: In stronger-debater/weaker-judge debates on programmatically verifiable code and logic tasks, the judge could check claims before ruling. For two model pairings in which the critic and the judge had similar binary-classification ability, the judge's verification rate was compared between transcripts with and without a critic's speech.
option_a: The judge's verification rate rose once a critic entered the transcript.
option_b: The judge's verification rate fell once a critic entered the transcript.
evidence_quote: On the two non-responder pairings in our set, debate produces null effects, and judge verification rates drop by tens of percentage points once a critic enters the transcript.
notes: Headline side = the critic/debate helps the judge (verification rises).

title: SLMJury: Can Small Language Models Judge as Well as Large Ones?
question: When small language model judges (0.6B-14B parameters) used a multi-round multi-agent debate protocol, was their judging accuracy higher or lower than without the protocol?
methods: Sixteen small language models from four families judged outputs on eight closed-ended reasoning benchmarks plus SummEval and MT-Bench. Judging accuracy under standard evaluation was compared with accuracy under a multi-agent debate protocol in which judges exchange and update their verdicts over several rounds.
option_a: Judging accuracy was higher under the debate protocol than without it.
option_b: Judging accuracy was lower under the debate protocol than without it.
evidence_quote: (4) Under the Reflect-Critique-Refine (RCR) debate protocol, multi-agent debate degrades accuracy across all tested configurations, whereas the top judges resist six adversarial personas with <=0.55% variance.
